The modern written form became established in Norwegian toward the end of the 19th century. It may have been introduced or reinforced through Danish pølse (“sausage”), whose Old Danish predecessor pylse (“sausage”) is attested since 1383, but the immediate route into Norwegian is not securely established. Ultimately unknown.

1000629.etyen:
Internationalism, ultimately from Latin Turcia (“Turkey”), from Medieval Greek Τουρκίᾱ (Tourkíā, “Turkey”), formed from Τοῦρκος (Toûrkos, “Turk”) and -ίᾱ (-íā, “country-name suffix”). The ethnonym was borrowed from Classical Persian ترک (“Turk”), from Middle Persian twlkʾ (turk, “Turk”), ultimately from Old Turkic 𐱅𐰇𐰼𐰜 (t²ẅr²ẅk², “Turk”), from Proto-Turkic *tür(ü)k (“Turk”), of uncertain further origin.
Compare the parallel international forms Danish Tyrkiet, Swedish Turkiet, German Türkei, Dutch Turkije, French Turquie and Turkish Türkiye (“Turkey”).

1003189.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Ancient Greek Ἰαπετός (Iapetós, “Iapetos”), possibly from Pre-Greek. The deeper origin of the name is uncertain.
The Latinized form is Iapetus, reflected in Norwegian Iapetus, the name used for the moon of Saturn and the prehistoric ocean named after the mythological Iapetos.
Compare Danish Iapetos, Finnish Iapetos, Estonian Iapetos and German Iapetos (“Iapetus”).

1003957.etyen:
Donald Duck + -isme, first part from English Donald Duck. Last part from French -isme (“-ism”), from Latin -isma, -ismus (“-ism”), from Ancient Greek -ισμός (-ismós, “forms abstract nouns”), from the suffix -μός (-mós, “forms abstract nouns”), from Proto-Indo-European *-mos or *-mós (“creates action/result nouns from verb stems”).
First used in writing by Norwegian author Jon Gisle in his book Donaldismen ("The Donaldism") (1973).

en.g: a neighborhood of Ullern borough, Oslo, Norway
a farm in Oslo, Norway, the historical farm from which the neighborhood and borough take their name

1004725.etyen:
Inherited from Old Norse Ullarin, from Ullar, the genitive of Ullr (“Ull”), and vin (“natural meadow, pasture”), hence “Ull's meadow”.
The name originally belonged to Ullern farm, which is first mentioned in 1357–1358. The surrounding neighborhood, parish and later administrative borough were named after the farm.

en.g: fixed-date bill; a bill of exchange payable on a specified calendar date
x: The fixed-date bill falls due for payment on 10 May.
Dagveksel eller presisveksel er en veksel hvis forfallsdag er presisert i teksten.
A fixed-date bill is a bill of exchange whose due date is specified in the text.

1004981.etyen:
dag (“day”) + veksel (“bill of exchange”), literally “day bill of exchange”.
With dag (“day”) being inherited from Old Norse dagr (“day”), from Proto-Germanic *dagaz (“day”), of uncertain further origin.
While veksel (“bill of exchange”) is borrowed from German Wechsel (“change, exchange; bill of exchange”), from Middle High German wëhsel, from Old High German wehsal, from Proto-Germanic *wihslaz (“change, exchange”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *weyk- (“to exchange, curve”).
Compare the parallel formations Danish dagveksel, Swedish dagväxel and German Tagwechsel (“fixed-date bill”).
